Book Text Faces

Five text faces with real small caps and old-style figures, each setting the same slice of the Paladin's page in the decided direction (B with the research only, trait lines kept). Only the text face changes; the cards stay in the same sans (Source Sans 3), with their Flavor in the text face's italic. Switches to dark with your system.

EB GaramondAlegreyaSource Serif 4LiterataVollkorn

EB Garamond

Georg Duffner's revival of Claude Garamont's 16th-century romans. The most classical of the five: the face of a printed book from before the age of print shops. Its x-height is small, so it is set a size larger here, and its strokes are thin on a screen, more so in dark mode.

Hallmark Action Selection

Choose one of the following Hallmark Actions. Both are Round Actions: each can be used once a round. Binding Light roots a foe for 1 round on a Tier 2 or 3; Lay On Hands gives an ally Guard equal to 2 + your Power Modifier, and at 2 AP lets them use 1 Rally Point.

Example. Lonny's Paladin has Power Modifier +2 and 20 Vigor. On round 3 he uses Binding Light against a goblin and rolls 17: a Tier 2. The goblin takes 1[W] + [Mod] and 1d6 Holy, and is Immobilized until the end of its next turn.

Binding LightRound · 2 AP
Your blow lands wreathed in light that roots your foe where it stands.

Tier 1[R] 1d6 Ho.
Tier 2[V] 1[W] + [Mod] + [R] 1d6 Ho; Immobilized (1 round).
Tier 3[V] 1[W] + [Mod] + [R] 1d8 Ho; Immobilized (1 round).

Unspent AP

If you end your turn without spending all your AP, you keep the rest until your next turn starts. Each AP you still had unused gives you GUARD for 1 round: 2 per AP at Stages 0 and 1, 3 at Stage 2 and 4 at Stage 3.

Alegreya

Juan Pablo del Peral, 2011, drawn for literature: calligraphic, lively, with a rhythm of the pen. It has a matching sans (Alegreya Sans) for the cards. The most character of the five without being costume.

Source Serif 4

Frank Grießhammer for Adobe, after Pierre-Simon Fournier's 18th-century types. Large x-height and optical sizes (the letters change for small text and headings), made for screens. Same family as the cards' sans (Source Sans 3). The plainest and clearest; less old.

Literata

TypeTogether, for Google Play Books: a face for long reading on screens, with optical sizes. Contemporary and sturdy; reads like a good modern novel more than an old book.

Vollkorn

Friedrich Althausen: "bread and butter" type, dark and sturdy, with an old-style warmth. Holds up well in dark mode. Its italic has no small caps (rarely needed).

Each face is embedded as a subset of its full file (Latin only), because the files Google Fonts serves strip the small caps and old-style figures. The book would carry the same files. The word GUARD in "Unspent AP" is set in small caps only to show them; it is not a proposal.
